Opposite Party
 Coram :- Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ratnaker Bhengra

For the Petitioner :- Mr. A.K. Das, Advocate
 For the State :- Mr. B.N. Ojha, App
 ...
Heard both the counsels.

The petitioner is an accused in this case for the offence registered under sections 376(AB), 376(2)(n)
& 377 of the Indian Penal Code as well as under sections 4/8/12 of the POCSO Act.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that allegations against the petitioner are falsely made.
The case of the prosecution is that the father of the child had taken loan amounting to Rs.3,50,000/- from the temple with which the petitioner is related.
There was some delay in returning the loan amount and, therefore, this case has been lodged.
Hence, the allegations are totally motivated against the petitioner.

The learned counsel has further submitted that the girl was medically examined and this is revealed in para-41 of the case diary that there is no sign of any injury found on the body, which would indicate that no offence of such nature was committed.
Moreover, the petitioner is in custody since 17.10.2022.
Therefore, the petitioner may be granted privilege of bail.

Learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the bail application of the petitioner and has submitted that the allegations in the FIR made by the father of the girl are enough and it cannot be said that the father would put his own girl to such allegations just for some monetary issue.
The learned counsel has further submitted that the statement of the victim-girl is fully supportive of the prosecution case.

Having gone through the records of the case and arguments in the facts and circumstances, I am not inclined to grant bail to the present petitioner, named above, in connection with POCSO Case No.
158 of 2022, arising out of Jagarnathpur PS Case No. 398 of 2022, pending in the Court of the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner-IV-cum-Spl. Judge, POCSO, Ranchi.
